status_summary: Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) extended the time limit on benefits for adults without dependents to ages 18 through 64, narrowed the child-based exemption to children under 14, removed the exemptions for veterans, people experiencing homelessness and former foster youth, and limited area waivers to unemployment of 10 percent or higher (with separate Alaska and Hawaii rules). The law also requires future Thrifty Food Plan re-evaluations to be cost neutral and limits the automatic heating and cooling utility allowance tied to energy assistance to households with an elderly or disabled member. USDA issued implementing memos in September and October 2025, and the hold-harmless period for state error rates ended 2025-11-01. A federal court in Rhode Island ordered USDA on 2025-10-31 to honor existing work-requirement waivers that USDA had moved to end early; that case was dismissed as moot in March 2026 after the waivers expired on 2026-03-01. A USDA draft rule to narrow broad-based categorical eligibility reached OMB on 2025-10-24, and no published proposal was found in the sources reviewed (which run through June 2026). USDA data show about 41.2 million participants in September 2025 and about 36.4 million in June 2026 (preliminary); the data do not establish the cause of the change.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed. Its SNAP sections (10101 to 10103) cap future Thrifty Food Plan increases, widen the adult work requirement and restrict waivers, and limit the utility allowance linked to energy assistance. Several provisions took effect on enactment.
FNS memo to state agencies summarizes the law's SNAP provisions: age limit raised, new exemption rules, waiver limits, cost-neutral Thrifty Food Plan adjustments, and utility allowance changes.

FNS issues an implementation memorandum on the revised ABAWD exceptions: time limit extended to ages 18 to 64, caregiver exception limited to children under 14, and the exceptions for veterans, people experiencing homelessness and former foster youth removed, effective on enactment (2025-07-04) and applied immediately at application and recertification.
A draft USDA proposed rule titled Reforming Categorical Eligibility is received by OMB for review. No conclusion date is listed.

In Rhode Island State Council of Churches v. Rollins (D.R.I., No. 1:25-cv-00569, Chief Judge John J. McConnell Jr.), brought by cities, faith-based and nonprofit groups, SNAP recipients and retailers, the court grants a temporary restraining order at a hearing and orders USDA to honor existing waivers of certain SNAP work requirements (written order ECF 19 dated 2025-11-01); the plaintiffs' motion of 2025-10-30 had sought to stay USDA's early termination of ABAWD waivers, effective 2025-11-02.

The 120-day quality-control variance exclusion period for the H.R. 1 work-requirement and standard utility allowance changes (sections 10102 and 10103) ends; FNS questions and answers of 2025-11-14 state that the period began 2025-07-04, ended 2025-11-01 and cannot be extended.

The parties in Rhode Island State Council of Churches v. Rollins (D.R.I., No. 1:25-cv-00569) file a joint stipulation of dismissal as moot after the waivers at issue expired on 2026-03-01; the Clearinghouse lists the case as closed on 2026-03-03.
USDA monthly data (preliminary) show about 36.4 million SNAP participants in June 2026, down from about 41.2 million in September 2025 (month-level date; exact release date not stated).

title: Tighten SNAP work requirements, categorical eligibility and utility allowances
uncertainties: Whether the categorical eligibility proposal has been published after June 2026 was not confirmed; a Federal Register search for FNS proposed and final rules since 2025-01-20 found none on categorical eligibility, and the OMB review entry is the only primary evidence. The NGA timeline is a secondary summary. The participation change is shown from USDA data without a causal finding; a local news article attributing it to rules effective 2026-02-01 was not verified and was not used. The shutdown-era benefit litigation and state-level implementation differences were not examined in detail. Because the Mandate proposed a regulatory path and the change came through a reconciliation law with a wider scope (ages to 64), the match is rated partial. A National Governors Association timeline lists five H.R. 1 SNAP provisions under the hold-harmless period and an FNS memo of 2025-09-04; only sections 10102 and 10103 are confirmed by the FNS memo opened on 2026-10-23, and the rest is an unverified lead. A Ballotpedia News item (2026-04-02), an unverified lead, reports that USDA guidance of 2026-02-26 reversed the early waiver terminations and let the affected waivers run to their original end dates; the Clearinghouse page for the Rhode Island case does not mention that guidance, and no USDA copy was found, so it is not a timeline event. Earlier text tied USDA's announcement of early waiver terminations to the 2025-10-03 memo, which does not mention waivers; the termination date of 2025-11-02 rests on the plaintiffs' motion. Checked 2026-10-31: a District of Oregon ruling of mid-September 2026 (22 states and the District of Columbia; Judge Kasubhai) held USDA's implementation deadline for some H.R. 1 eligibility-calculation changes unlawful and set aside guidance excluding certain lawful permanent residents, per Supermarket News; the reports read do not say whether it reaches the work-requirement provisions or the 2025-11-01 end of the quality-control hold-harmless period, and the ruling itself was not read.
